title: JPL DE backend: mmap reader + header parse
description:
Port the JPL DE binary file open + header parse (swejpl.c `fsizer` / `state` first-call init) as a stateless, mmap-backed reader. No Chebyshev interpolation in this sub-task — that is the next sub-task.

Read `docs/c-ref-jpl.md` first (whole doc; this sub-task uses §Constants, §Data Structures, §File Format, §"Byte Order / Endianness", §`fsizer`).

## Architecture invariants (non-negotiable)
- Stateless: `JplFile` holds read-only data (mmap + parsed header). All methods take `&self`. No `&mut self`, no interior mutability, no cached-record field. The OS page cache + mmap replaces C's mutable record cache.
- Backend isolation (sutra forbidden_dep, severity=blocking): the `jpl` module MUST NOT import from `sweph_file` or `moshier`. Define its own byte-order reader; do not reuse `sweph_file::types::ByteOrder`. The minor duplication is required by the independence constraint.
- Use mmap, NOT BufReader (the file `ephe/de441.eph` is 2.7 GB).

## Files
- Convert `src/jpl.rs` (currently an empty stub) into a directory module:
  - `src/jpl/mod.rs` — declares submodules; defines `JplFile` (mmap + `JplHeader`), `JplFile::open`, accessors. Re-export `JplHeader`.
  - `src/jpl/header.rs` — local `ByteOrder` enum + `Reader`, endian detection, header parse, ksize computation, `JplHeader` struct.
  - To convert: `mv src/jpl.rs /tmp/` is blocked by policy; instead create `src/jpl/mod.rs` and `src/jpl/header.rs`. The empty `src/jpl.rs` and the new `src/jpl/` cannot coexist — ask Josh to remove the empty `src/jpl.rs`, or (preferred) keep a single-file `src/jpl.rs` ONLY IF you also place header code inline; but the dir-module layout mirroring `sweph_file/` is the target. Coordinate the one-file deletion with Josh (file deletion is on the auto-deny list).
- `src/lib.rs`: `pub mod jpl;` already present (line 16); a directory module resolves identically — no edit needed.
- Update the backend-isolation constraint patterns: the forbidden_dep constraints (provenance `yojana:swisseph-rs §module-tree`) reference `src/jpl.rs`; once jpl becomes a directory they go inert (zero-match), silently disabling isolation enforcement. Update the module-tree source so the patterns read `src/jpl/**` (mirror the same fix needed for `src/sweph_file/**`). Note this in the execution_record.
- Tests: `tests/golden/jpl_header.rs` (new), `tests/c-gen/gen_jpl_header.c` (new), register `mod jpl_header;` in `tests/golden/main.rs`.

## Implementation steps

1. **`ByteOrder` + `Reader`** (header.rs). Define `enum ByteOrder { Little, Big }` with `read_i16/read_i32/read_f64(&self, bytes) -> _` (swap iff Big). Define a `Reader<'a> { data: &'a [u8], pos: usize, order: ByteOrder }` with `read_i32/read_f64/skip/seek` and bounds checks returning `Error::FileFormat`. Mirror the shape of `sweph_file/parse.rs`'s `Reader` but write it fresh inside jpl. Cite c-ref-jpl.md §"reorder()".

2. **Endian detection** (c-ref-jpl.md §"Detection Strategy"). JPL files have NO magic number. Read `ss[0..3]` (3 f64 at byte offset 2652) as Little-endian; if `ss[2] < 1.0 || ss[2] > 200.0`, the file is Big-endian → re-read as Big. Validate plausibility: `ss[0],ss[1]` ∈ [-5_583_942.0, 9_025_909.0], `ss[2]` ∈ [1.0, 200.0]; else `Error::FileFormat`.

3. **Header parse** (c-ref-jpl.md §"Record 0 — File Header" offset table). From the mmap with the detected order: skip 252 (title) + 2400 (cnam) = offset 2652; read `ss[3]`; read `ncon: i32` @2676; `au: f64` @2680; `emrat: f64` @2688; `ipt[0..36]` (36 × i32) @2696; `numde: i32` @2840; `lpt[0..3]` (3 × i32) @2844, copy into `ipt[36..39]`. Result: `ipt: [i32; 39]`.

4. **ksize computation** (c-ref-jpl.md §`fsizer`). DE441 is NOT in the known-ksize table — compute generically: iterate `i in 0..13`, track `kmx`/`khi` = (max `ipt[i*3]`, `i+1`); `nd = if khi == 12 { 2 } else { 3 }`; `ksize = ((ipt[khi*3-3] + nd*ipt[khi*3-2]*ipt[khi*3-1] - 1) * 2) as usize`; if `ksize == 1546 { ksize = 1652 }`; validate `1000 <= ksize <= 5000`. Derive `irecsz = 4*ksize` (bytes), `ncoeffs = ksize/2` (doubles per record).

5. **File-length validation** (c-ref-jpl.md §"File Validation" step 1). Compute `nseg = ((ss[1]-ss[0])/ss[2])` segments; expected coefficient doubles = Σ over bodies `i in 0..12` of `ipt[i*3+1]*ipt[i*3+2]*(if i==11 {2} else {3})*nseg`, plus `2*nseg` (start/end JD per segment), ×8 bytes, plus `2*ksize*4` (header+constants records). Accept `mmap.len() == expected` OR `expected + ksize*4`. Else `Error::FileFormat`.

6. **`JplFile::open(path: &Path)`** (mod.rs). Open file, mmap with `unsafe { Mmap::map(&file) }` and the same SAFETY comment as `SwissEphFile::open` (src/sweph_file/mod.rs:28-32). Parse header (steps 2-5). Store `mmap` + `header`. Provide `&self` accessors: `header() -> &JplHeader`, `bytes() -> &[u8]`, `byte_order() -> ByteOrder` (so the next sub-task can read records). Add a `_assert_send_sync` test like sweph_file/mod.rs:143.

## `JplHeader` (pub, in header.rs)
```rust
pub struct JplHeader {
    pub byte_order: ByteOrder,
    pub ss: [f64; 3],   // [start_jd, end_jd, seg_days]
    pub au: f64,        // AU in km
    pub emrat: f64,     // Earth/Moon mass ratio
    pub denum: i32,     // DE number (expect 441)
    pub ncon: i32,
    pub ipt: [i32; 39], // 13 bodies × 3 (offset[1-based], ncf, na)
    pub ksize: usize,
    pub irecsz: usize,  // bytes per record
    pub ncoeffs: usize, // doubles per record
}
```

## C reference
`docs/c-ref-jpl.md` §§ Constants, Data Structures, File Format, "Byte Order / Endianness", `fsizer`, "File Validation".

## Golden tests
- **`gen_jpl_header.c`** (standalone parser, NOT linked against libswe internals — model on `tests/c-gen/gen_se1_header.c`): open `ephe/de441.eph` with `fopen`/`fread`, replicate the header parse independently, and emit `tests/golden-data/jpl_header.json` with `{ ss:[3], au, emrat, denum, ncon, ipt:[39], ncoeffs }`. Build/run instructions in a header comment matching gen_se1_header.c.
  - Use the absolute path `<repo>/ephe/de441.eph` (NOT `../swisseph/ephe`, which has no `.eph` file).
- **`jpl_header.rs`**: locate `ephe/de441.eph` via `PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("ephe").join("de441.eph")`. If `!path.exists()` → `return` (skip, gated on file presence). Else open `JplFile`, deserialize the JSON, assert: `ss` exact (assert_f64_exact), `au` exact, `emrat` exact, `denum == 441`, `ncon`, `ipt[39]` element-wise exact, `ncoeffs` matches.

## Acceptance criteria
- `cargo build` clean.
- `cargo test --test golden jpl_header -- --nocapture` passes (de441.eph IS present, so it must actually run and pass — a silent skip is a failure to report).
- `cargo clippy --all-targets` — no new warnings.
- `mcp__sutra__sutra_constraints action=violations` shows no new blocking forbidden_dep violations from the jpl module.

## Escape hatch
If header fields mismatch the C reference after two debugging attempts, STOP and report: which fields, actual vs expected (esp. ksize/ncoeffs and ipt[]), and the endian-detection outcome. The most likely culprits are endian detection and the 1-based ipt offsets. Escalate to Opus.
execution_record: Straightforward port. Two non-obvious points: (1) serde doesn't implement Deserialize for [i32; 39] (max is 32), so the golden test uses Vec<i32> instead; (2) the file-length validation loop must cover all 13 bodies (0..13) including librations — the ref doc's 'for i in 0..12' notation is inclusive/13-body, not exclusive/12-body. Confirmed by checking that sum-of-body-coefficients + 2 JDs per segment × 8 bytes + 2 header records × ksize×4 equals the actual 2.7 GB file size. Backend-isolation constraints now bind (all four jpl-touching constraints show non-zero matched_file_count, zero violations)."
